title: Removal of gDNA from total RNA
author: Igem Dusseldorf
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8bfhsjn
materials: discard supernatant, remove as much ethanol as possible

steps.title: Prepare DNase I Reaction
steps.instruction: Assemble the reaction components in a RNase-free 1.5 ml tube in the following order: H2O (up to 10 µl), buffer (1 µl), total RNA (1 µg), and DNaseI (1 µl).

steps.title: Incubate for gDNA Digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Inactivate DNase I
steps.instruction: Add 1 µl of 50 mM EDTA and incubate at 65°C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA
steps.instruction: Add 1/10 volume of NaOAc and 3 volumes of 100% EtOH to the mixture.

steps.title: Freeze Sample
steps.instruction: Freeze the sample at -20°C overnight or at -80°C for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Centrifuge and Collect Pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13,000 rpm at 4°C for 30 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Align the tube lid to mark the location of the RNA pellet, as it may be invisible

steps.title: Wash RNA Pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet with 500 µl of 70% EtOH.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13,000 rpm at 4°C for 10 minutes

steps.title: Dry and Resuspend RNA
steps.instruction: Dry the tubes at room temperature (RT) under the hood for approximately 5 minutes, ensuring not to overdry.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 20 µl RNase-free water

steps.title: Quantify and Verify RNA
steps.instruction: Measure the RNA concentration and verify the removal of gDNA via PCR.

substeps.instruction: Perform PCR on the DNA-free RNA
Include a positive control using gDNA as a template and a primer that binds to it
Confirm that no visible bands appear except for the positive control
